# DiscoPoP B19 and B18 — a wrong `lastprivate` in three places and the Do-All that nests with counters declared at the top of the function had lost: the repairs and their regression check

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

After the explorer's repairs of 8 Oct (a last value assigned in only some passes blocks Do-All; an array is shared; only a loop's own units decide its clauses; a write-after-read is attached to units by its own roles): does DiscoPoP alone give every one of the 44 tsvc_c3 packages its measured class, with a difference only where the repairs aim (s331, s481), and what does it now say on the 31 packages outside TSVC?

## Result in one paragraph

Passed on TSVC: on the 44 tsvc_c3 packages every class and every draw is as before the repairs; DiscoPoP offers other directives on the two loops the repairs aim at and nowhere else (s331: nothing offered any more; s481: the kept directive without lastprivate(nl)). Outside TSVC, correlation, covariance and fdtd-2d have their outer loop's directive back in 3 of 3 draws (medians 5.7×, 5.7×, 4.2×) — nine loops given back by the B18 repair, none lost. Two things the draws showed that are not the repairs': on PolyBench the explorer, on one profile, blocks every loop that carries an observed dependence or none of them, never a part, and blocks none in 57 of 81 profiles (B21, measured, not traced) — gramschmidt's loop comes back only in such draws (2 of 3); and a rule of DiscoPoP's own calls a loop parallel whose pass reads an array element a later pass overwrites (B22, new: adi's last nest, refused by the gate in 3 of 3 draws; on TSVC hidden by B16). One regression of the array repair showed in those draws, on burkardt/md (the force loop's work array rij shared where each thread needs its own; refused by the gate) and was corrected the same day: an array that a function the loop calls writes keeps its private clause. RE-CHECK on the corrected explorer, six more draws (t0_11_c3_b19r_a–c, t0_11_b19r_apps_a–c): the 44 TSVC packages as on the first repair in every class, outcome, directive, clause and verdict; md's loop with its private work array again in 3 of 3 draws; what else differs outside TSVC is draw-to-draw (B21 and the order of DiscoPoP's patterns), not the correction. After nine draws: the explorer blocks all such loops in 65 PolyBench profiles, none in 133, some in 0; five kernels never seen blocking. A blocked loop's record names one of the loop's dependences and which one differs between runs — the variable on 40 of 44 TSVC packages, on s244 also the type. Found on the way, in our own gate: its dependence stage compares the working file's line numbers with the profile's and refused one correct directive on mvt (its only refusal in the whole archive; the repair and what it changes are planned with E7). No model in any of it.

| 2026-10-08 | finding | **The gate's dependence stage compares line numbers of two different files: once a directive has been kept, the next directive below it is judged against the dependences of the loop one line further down. Found in tonight's draws on `polybench/mvt` — a correct DiscoPoP directive refused. In the whole archive the stage refused this once; how often it missed a dependence is not measured; nothing is changed yet.** **What happened** (`t0_11_b19r_apps_a`, `polybench/mvt`, DiscoPoP alone): the kernel is two nests side by side, `for (i…) for (j…) x1[i] = x1[i] + A[i][j] * y_1[j];` (lines 76–78) and the same for `x2` (lines 79–81). Both outer loops are parallel — each `i` has its own `x1[i]` — and DiscoPoP reports both as Do-All and both inner loops as blocked (the read-after-write on `x1[i]`, on `x2[i]`). The first directive is kept. The second is refused at the stage `dependences`: "DiscoPoP OBSERVED 1 loop-carried dependence(s) in lines 79-81 that prevent a Do-All: RAW on x2[] in the loop at line 80". The loop at line 80 is the INNER loop; the directive is on the loop at line 79. **Why:** the stage takes the directive's loop from the patch (`annotated_loop_lines`), and the patch is made against the working file, which already holds the first directive — one line more above the second nest. So the patch says "line 80" for what the profile calls line 79, and the blocker records (`explorer/doall_prevented.json`) are in the profile's numbering. Run on the archived patches: the stage reads the first directive's loop as line 76 (right) and the second's as line 80 (the profile's 79). **In both directions:** a correct directive is refused when the loop the shifted number points at is blocked on an observed dependence (here: the inner loop, one line down); and an observed dependence on the directive's own loop would be missed by this stage (ThreadSanitizer and the schedule matrix still run). **Width:** all 3020 archived candidate files of the campaign searched for a candidate refused at this stage: 1, this one. (Corrected 9 Oct, two rows up: that search matched 3,020 of the archive's 3,469 candidate files; over all 3,469 — 14,200 candidates — the count is the same, 1.) It needs a directive kept above in the same file AND an observed blocker on the loop the shifted line points at; on most PolyBench draws the explorer records no observed blocker at all (B21), on this draw it recorded all of them. The trial ended `parallel-speed-not-measurable` with one directive instead of two (1.1× against 2.8–4.2× in the first repair's three draws). No agent trial, no model-alone trial and no earlier draw of DiscoPoP alone holds a refusal by this stage. The other direction is NOT measured: a directive below an accepted one whose own loop carried an observed dependence would have passed this stage; ThreadSanitizer and the schedule matrix ran on every such candidate, so the stage alone cannot have let a race through. **Why it matters now:** the next experiment (E7) measures the gate as a classifier — this is a wrong verdict of the gate with a known cause. **Proposed, not done:** the repair (the patch's lines translated to the profile's numbering, with a check that fails before and passes after), under its own row; no text a model reads is involved. **When** is part of E7's design and decided with it: E7 measures the gate that produced the campaign's verdicts, so a repair before it changes the instrument under study; measured as it ran, E7 can replay the repaired stage on every saved directive and count what the defect changed in either direction **(9 Oct: E7 is set aside by the author for now; the repair is decided with E3's design, on the count taken from the archive — rows of 9 Oct above.)** | Finding, gate dependence stage |
